d:Silverline.SL_PolicyDef/SL_LegalShield: 80 % of every fine, and an appeal is lodged.
The whole fine. Advocate Brix reads your forms before you do.
Fines and penalties of inspectors, licence trouble and collection disputes. Also lowers the chance that Clawback Mutual denies your claims, and fixes your cancellation forms.
The claims department looks at your claim one day sooner.
Linear by the Schedule of Limbs, from 20 % invalidity. Partial losses are not paid.
225 % progression from 5 % invalidity. Partial losses are paid.
350 % progression from 1 % invalidity. Every finger has a price.
One colonist. Permanent consequences of accidents by the Schedule of Limbs, and accidental death (20 % of the sum). Assessed one quadrum after the accident. Operations are not accidents.
Premium accidents pay on the 500 % table instead of 350 %. Only matters for the big ones.
The accidental death sum rises from 20 % to 30 % of the basic sum.
d:Silverline.SL_PolicyDef/SL_MuffaloMach: Repair money, half of the time value.
Cash or parts by capsule, 80 % of the time value.
Replacement value, instantly. The tow drone is yours.
Shuttles, drop pods and vehicles destroyed by hostile forces. Bionic parts are equipment and are, in principle, also meant to be here. In practice: see the Accident Plan.
Pays 10 % more of every loss (never more than the loss itself).
d:Silverline.SL_PolicyDef/SL_RimHealth.b: 10 silver per bedridden colonist and day, up to 5 days in 15.
15 silver per bedridden colonist and day, up to 5 days in 15.
25 silver per bedridden colonist and day, up to 5 days in 15. The second opinion is free.
d:Silverline.SL_PolicyDef/SL_RimHealth.c: Every day a colonist is bedridden with an illness or an injury that needs treatment, but at most 5 paid days per colonist in any 15 days (the hospital-indemnity cap). Food poisoning is an accident of cooking and counts anyway.
d:Silverline.SL_PolicyDef/SL_RimHealth.r: Pays 10 % more on every sickbed day.
d:Silverline.SL_PolicyDef/SL_RoofOverHea: Cash for the burnt building, after your own share.
Cash, or building materials by capsule.
Replacement value, instantly by capsule. Ashes not included.
Buildings of your colony destroyed by fire, explosions and storms. Fires and blasts started by your own people are excluded (§11).
Pays 10 % more of every loss (never more than the loss itself).
The claims department looks at your claim one day sooner.
d:Silverline.SL_PolicyDef/SL_Unspeakable: Cash, after your own share. Please do not describe the entity.
Replacement value, instantly. A specialist is on the phone.
The sum per head, only if somebody dies on the road.
Death, and lost body parts by the Schedule of Limbs.
Everything above, and a flat sum for every single injury.
Colonists on caravans. Bare Minimum pays only a death, Good Enough also lost body parts, Premium every scratch.
d:TraitDef/HH_BornHost.degreeDatas.0.des: {PAWN_nameDef} remembers names, refills glasses before they are empty and makes strangers feel expected. Learns hosting faster.
d:TraitDef/HH_Caregiver.degreeDatas.0.de: {PAWN_nameDef} sits with the sick and notices who is not eating. Massages {PAWN_pronoun} gives do more good, and children and families {PAWN_pronoun} welcomes or shows around are a little happier.
d:TraitDef/HH_EagleEye.degreeDatas.0.des: {PAWN_nameDef} notices who wanders where they should not. While {PAWN_pronoun} is on the map, respectable guests stumble on the back room less often.
d:TraitDef/HH_Gambler.degreeDatas.0.desc: {PAWN_nameDef} loves the table: the spin, the shuffle, the pause before the card turns. Gambling is more fun, and more dangerous, for {PAWN_objective}. As a guest {PAWN_pronoun} brings a bigger bankroll and bets bigger, and at blackjack and poker {PAWN_pronoun} plays a little sharper.
d:TraitDef/HH_GamblingAverse.degreeDatas: {PAWN_nameDef} refuses to gamble, never gets hooked, and is uneasy in rooms where the house takes bets.
d:TraitDef/HH_Gossip.degreeDatas.0.descr: {PAWN_nameDef} cannot keep a story to {PAWN_objective}self. When guests leave, what they tell others moves the house's renown further, good or bad.
d:TraitDef/HH_Gossip.degreeDatas.0.label: gossip
d:TraitDef/HH_Grump.degreeDatas.0.descri: {PAWN_nameDef} runs the front desk like a customs post. Guests {PAWN_pronoun} chats with come away a little less happy.
d:TraitDef/HH_Grump.degreeDatas.0.label: grump
d:TraitDef/HH_KidMagnet.degreeDatas.0.de: Children follow {PAWN_nameDef} around like ducklings. Children and families {PAWN_pronoun} welcomes or shows around are happier.
d:TraitDef/HH_Lucky.degreeDatas.0.descri: {PAWN_nameDef} has a knack for landing on the right side of a coin. At the casino's house games {PAWN_pronoun} plays with a slightly kinder payout plan, and two winning sessions in a row are enough for a lucky streak. While {PAWN_pronoun} lives in the colony, every tenth lottery ticket the colony buys is free.
d:TraitDef/HH_Lucky.degreeDatas.0.label: lucky
d:TraitDef/HH_Peacemaker.degreeDatas.0.d: {PAWN_nameDef} steps between raised voices and turns them down again. Quarrels in the same room as {PAWN_objective} turn into fistfights less often.
d:TraitDef/HH_PennyPincher.degreeDatas.0: {PAWN_nameDef} reads every line of every contract, twice. While {PAWN_pronoun} lives in the colony, the bank charges 20 % lower fees. Guests find the prices a little steep when {PAWN_pronoun} serves them.
d:TraitDef/HH_SilverTongue.degreeDatas.0: {PAWN_nameDef} could talk a river into a different bed. Guests expect a little less after {PAWN_pronoun} welcomes them at the front desk or shows them around, and a guest who joins the colony costs less goodwill when {PAWN_pronoun} is the one who won them over.
{PAWN_nameDef}'s fingers do not shake. As a croupier {PAWN_pronoun} deals noticeably faster.
d:TraitDef/HH_Unlucky.degreeDatas.0.desc: {PAWN_nameDef} drops toast butter-side down. At the casino's house games the payout plan runs slightly worse for {PAWN_objective}, and every lost session stings.
